topic: Unbound KV Caches Choke On-Prem LLM Concurrency
postText:
Deploying local LLMs in healthcare IT sounds simple until three doctors summarize long patient charts at the exact same second.

Everything looked great in isolated testing. We stood up an open-source 70B parameter model on dual 24GB GPUs for automated clinical note extraction. Latency was acceptable. Precision was high. Then day one of on-prem testing hit: three concurrent EHR requests arrived, and the GPU threw a fatal CUDA Out-of-Memory error.

The culprit was not model weight footprint. It was the unmanaged KV cache.

In standard inference, context tokens reserve static memory slots across full context lengths. Unused pre-allocated buffers cause massive VRAM fragmentation. When multiple streams hit the engine simultaneously, available VRAM vanishes even if actual token throughput is low.

Here is how we stabilized our local inference runtime:
1. PagedAttention: Splitting KV cache into virtual non-contiguous memory blocks (via vLLM) eliminated internal fragmentation and doubled concurrent serving capacity.
2. Continuous Dynamic Batching: Switching from static prompt batching to iteration-level batching ensured short lab queries were not stuck waiting for complex discharge summaries.
3. AWQ 4-Bit Quantization: Retaining outlier channels preserved medical precision while cutting weight footprint by 60%.

Compute is rarely your real production LLM bottleneck. Memory allocation architecture is.

How do you handle KV cache starvation and VRAM limits when hosting LLMs locally on edge hardware?
